plan.summary: Articles filed under 2+ shows with one shared pull quote (audit-shared-url-quote.js): give each show its own section quote and score, flag misfiled copies, human-clear flags that misread a multi-show column. Part 4 of 6.

actions.description: BRO-4599 human clear: text contains the Old Times (2015 Broadway, Hodge) section; prior CV flag misread the roundup

actions.oldValue: CV-promoted: The scraped content is primarily a review of 'Fool for Love' (wrong production entirely), with only a truncated fragment about 'Old Times' at the very end. The expected review should be exclusively ab
actions.newValue: BRO-4599: cleared; multi-show roundup whose Old Times section reviews this 2015 Broadway revival

actions.oldValue: Here, though, Rockwell and Arianda gleefully tear into one another, generating palpable sexual tension and nailing the grimly comic underbelly of Shepard's dialogue.
actions.newValue: But the three actors' performance styles -- Owen, cool and remote; Reilly, pixieish and flirty; Best, diva-scaled and emotive -- never mesh.
BRO-4599: Old Times section is negative: underpowered lead, styles never mesh, director's choices throw everything at the wall.

actions.description: article is about Once Upon a Mattress, a different show (currently mislabeled as wrongProduction)
BRO-4599 human clear: mis-flag: review explicitly covers the Hudson Theatre Broadway revival with Foster, matching this show id

actions.oldValue: Both arrive with clarity and purpose, and both serve as reminders of what the Broadway musical, carefully wrought, can accomplish.
actions.newValue: It’s a rare musical that can make you laugh so hard while also sneaking up on you with moments that catch you off-guard with their emotional power.
actions.description: joint closing quote replaced with Mincemeat section quote

actions.newValue: BRO-4599: Our Town section is a rave: production called a balm, ensemble whole greater than parts.

actions.oldValue: The real reason this production works is the acting, especially the two leads and two actors in smaller roles.
actions.newValue: Once the show is over, the plot logic, you realize, was a bit wonky, but for those who love this kind of stuff, the activity onstage is goofy, paranormal fun.

actions.oldValue: Plainly speaking, this Twelfth Night is a triumph.
actions.newValue: His Richard, while consistently entertaining, throws the play's more tragic elements somewhat off-balance, particularly in the many (more serious) scenes when he's off stage.
BRO-4599: Richard III section is positive with reservations: comic Richard unbalances tragedy, but well worth seeing.

actions.description: BRO-4599 human clear: mis-flag: article has a full Richard III section; caller may drop if already-flagged files must stay untouched

actions.oldValue: They achieve a spectacle of surpassing elegance and buoyancy: We see a classic comedy and a bloody tragedy in their pure Shakespearean glory.
actions.newValue: Rylance’s reading is so unfeigned, so childlike in its simplicity, we almost feel sympathy for the devil.

actions.oldValue: “Our Town,” unfolding at the Ethel Barrymore Theatre like a glorious hymn, was the play I didn’t realize just how badly our country needed right now.
actions.newValue: Gold’s “Romeo + Juliet” similarly succeeds more theatrically than dramatically.
BRO-4599: Romeo + Juliet section is mixed: lively, leads radiant, but doubling dizzying, chemistry thin, tragedy lost in hyperactive staging.

actions.description: Smash sections: strong belters but thin, flat, purposeless

actions.newValue: BRO-4599: Joint review. Smash sections: powerhouse singers but thinly conceived, flat sitcom rhythms, no verve; negative, 40.

actions.description: BRO-4599 human clear: fullText has a full Sondheim on Sondheim review section

BRO-4599: December 2023 Phoenix Theatre London review, not the 2025 Marquis Broadway production

actions.oldValue: But the story grabbed me, as teenage Kim works in a sex club run by a raunchy character known as the Engineer, falling for an American GI, Chris, who feels she deserves better.
actions.newValue: Nottage won the Pulitzer for Ruined, and with this, her first Broadway play, she’s achieved something earnest but worthwhile.
